cited_title: OpenScientist focused acgA GO:0001653 hypothesis report

cited_title: OpenScientist assessment of CAR4 adenylate-cyclase-activating signaling
review_notes: Primary assay scope and the explicit unpublished 1997 observation were verified. cited_title: Genetic interactions of the E3 ubiquitin ligase component FbxA with cyclic AMP metabolism and a histidine kinase signaling pathway during Dictyostelium discoideum development.
review_notes: Solid genetic evidence linking dhkA to RegA/cAMP and sporulation. The authors' proposed directionality (that DhkA activates RegA phosphodiesterase) explicitly contradicts Wang et al. (PMID:10373524 / PMID:15897458), who show ligand binding to DhkA inhibits phosphorelay to RegA; the direction of DhkA-RegA regulation is therefore contested. Hand-curated expert assessment - the Wang/Anjard-Loomis inhibition model is the better-supported working model. DhkA autophosphorylation on His1395 and phosphorelay through RdeA to the RegA receiver aspartate are biochemically demonstrated, and SDF-2 binding lowers this relay so RegA is dephosphorylated and inactivated, raising intracellular cAMP and activating PKA to trigger encapsulation. The fbxA genetic-interaction study reported here infers the opposite direction only indirectly, so it is recorded as a contested minority interpretation pending direct measurement of the RegA phosphorylation state in dhkA-null versus SDF-2-treated cells.

cited_title: PdsA/DdPDE1 (DICDI, UniProt P12019) — Adjudication of two negative-regulation GO claims
review_notes: Pool distinction and feedback biology are supported, but direct-only restriction on a regulation BP is unjustified; report itself admits no PdsA-specific PKA test or verified absence of a glucose-GPCR pathway. Fungal source papers not full-text read. Claimed GO:1902660 annotation is absent from this review and not used. PTN002001416 is a node in PTHR28283, not a family identifier. cited_title: Focused OpenScientist assessment of Dictyostelium PTEN nuclear localization and cell-cycle regulation
review_notes: Full substantive report read. It incorrectly calls GO:0051726 absent, despite the source IBA and PTN000959472 IBD; equates nonnuclear-positive imaging with nuclear exclusion; and treats cytokinesis as outside cell-cycle scope. Its low-confidence K289-to-E pairwise alignment has no delivered code/alignment output and does not establish a loss phenotype in Dictyostelium. The cited human K289E defect is rescuable by forced monoubiquitination. PMID:15809030 abstract describes lines lacking both enzymatic activities, whereas the report asserts pten loss with intact PI3K. Retain the mechanistic lead as a question rather than proof.

cited_title: OpenScientist focused rasC GO:0044351 hypothesis report
review_notes: The assertion of no RasC deletion/uptake evidence contradicts PMID:15878331. Failure to rescue RasG-dependent suspension growth is not identical to a direct negative macropinocytic mechanism assay. Reported pairwise sequence identities do not locate a functional gain/loss on the PAINT tree, and no executed alignment artifact was delivered.

cited_title: OpenScientist focused regA GO:0047555 hypothesis report
review_notes: The report omits PMID:34063491 and does not reconcile the greater-than selectivity bound in PMID:12429832 with the later ~200 claim. Another enzyme performing cGMP turnover does not establish its absence in RegA. Artifact evidence-tier plots are hardcoded summaries, not a new enzymatic or phylogenetic analysis.

cited_title: OpenScientist assessment of STATa proliferation regulation and defense response
review_notes: Read complete substantive report. Correctly distinguishes proliferation from differentiation and defense from osmotic stress; correctly identifies STATb among ancestral evidence. Rejection nevertheless rests on donor taxonomic composition, alternative pathway genes and missing target assays. It explicitly acknowledges untested target growth/defense and establishes no STATa-specific loss.

cited_title: AIGR Gene Hypothesis Deep Research — Dictyostelium discoideum statC (Q54BD4)
review_notes: Primary source leads and noncanonical stress activation are supported. Refuted verdict is not: report admits statC proliferation and bacterial-clearance roles are untested, treats paralog descendants as automatic propagation error, and adds JAK/cytokine requirements absent from the broad GO definitions. TirA/NADPH oxidase necessity does not exclude a STAT transcriptional regulator. No target-specific loss is established.

cited_title: ketu mutant mice uncover an essential meiotic function for the ancient RNA helicase YTHDC2.
review_notes: Full cached entry read; the paper supports mammalian YTHDC2 activity and a Bgcn-centric Drosophilidae phylogeny. cited_title: OpenScientist assessment of Dic4 thiamine pyrophosphate transport
review_notes: Read substantive findings and limitations. cited_title: Falcon deep research report on Hsp23 (Drosophila melanogaster)
review_notes: Full narrative, table and references read. Its suggestion that direct Hsp23 biochemistry remains a gap overlooks purified-client PMID:16572729. Its 2016 muscle-protection lead is verified in full PMID:27483356: perinuclear ubiquitin puncta are clients/aggregates, not proof of Hsp23 nuclear import.

cited_title: Purification and properties of a debranching enzyme from Escherichia coli.
review_notes: The identifier is correct and the abstract reports limit-dextrin alpha-1,6 hydrolysis, but the 1976 purified activity was not assigned to glgX and its weak glycogen activity conflicts with the later GlgX deletion and substrate-specificity work.

cited_title: A dual function of the CRISPR-Cas system in bacterial antivirus immunity and DNA repair.
review_notes: Verified against the cached PMC full text; the title, author list and journal match and the biochemical and structural results on YgbT/Cas1 are reported as the GOA rows describe them. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because the paper's second headline claim - a dedicated DNA-repair function for Cas1 - has not been corroborated in the fifteen years since, and the branched-DNA nuclease activities it reports were subsequently reinterpreted as the integrase active site catalysing disintegration. The biochemistry and the crystal structure are sound; the functional interpretation of them is the contested part, which is why the three annotations it supports are demoted rather than removed.

Cited here for the architecture, and for the record of the disagreement; the paper is on the Acidaminococcus ortholog, not this protein.

cited_title: Abundance and size of hyaluronan in naked mole-rat tissues and plasma.
review_notes: Full text cached and read. Correctly cited and methodologically careful (two independent sizing methods, quantitative cortex/medulla separation), but marked DISPUTED because its central size result directly contradicts PMID:23783513 and the discrepancy is unresolved - PMID:34476892 attributes it to isolation procedure. That dispute concerns polymer size only; the renal cortex/medulla quantification, which is what this review leans on for the two rat-derived annotations, is not contested by anyone and is the only such measurement in existence for this species.

Retain the report as provenance, not as negative functional evidence.

cited_title: Human A3GALT2 enzyme constructs and glycan substrate specificity: focused OpenScientist report
review_notes: Full report and four artifacts read. Its pivotal claim that PMID:23378701 contains no human positive experiment was inferred from the pig-focused abstract and is contradicted by full Methods, Figure 6 and Table 1. It also overlooks Figure 5 reverse-mutant experiments in PMID:18630988. Q3V1N9 is mouse, not rat: human U3KPV4 N253 aligns to rat A0A4Z3 Y252 and mouse Q3V1N9 Y283 in sequence version 1. The reported sequence identities/GTEx values lack reproducible raw artifacts. The source studies genuinely disagree in construct and assay scope; the report does not resolve the NOT or independently establish LacNAc exclusion.

cited_title: AADAC deacetylates PHEN
review_notes: The event supports phenacetin deacetylation. Its model places the small-molecule participants in cytosol while the AADAC catalytic bulk is lumen-facing at the ER, so the reaction geometry is internally inconsistent even though the activity is correct.

cited_title: AAK1 regulates Numb function at an early step in clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
review_notes: The cached abstract supports the reported Numb localization and cargo-selective phenotypes, but the central Numb-T102 substrate claim is contradicted by PMID:42082516: purified AAK1/BMP2K did not phosphorylate the site, RPE phosphoproteomics did not detect it, and its sequence lacks the refined recognition motif. Preserve the localization phenotype; do not treat T102 phosphorylation as established.

cited_title: Yeast models for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease-causing aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase alleles reveal the cellular basis of disease.
review_notes: The PubMed identity and recovered full PMC11953622 review were checked. Its AARS1 section usefully distinguishes yeast ALA1 complementation, human cytosolic function and allele-dependent assay limitations. It is a review, not a new direct human activity experiment. The generalization that human AlaRS is predominantly monomeric under normal cellular conditions is not adopted: the original purified-protein observation and separately examined humanized-yeast interference data have different assay scopes, as documented for PMID:7654687 and PMID:40491354. This assessment disputes that generalization, not the bibliographic identity or the existence of the reported yeast phenotypes.

cited_title: The role of Alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 lactylation in tumors and other diseases.
review_notes: Primary PubMed identity and full PMC12961078 review inspected. Bibliographic identity is correct, but the disease-mechanism narrative is not used as independent evidence: Figure 1 and the body expand ALSP differently, and its detailed proofreading/ER-stress disease claims require their original experimental sources. The newly cached biallelic series PMID:34446925 is independently scoped and is not equated to every adult-onset leukoencephalopathy claim. This flags the review narrative and nomenclature, without rejecting the separately established AARS1 charging or conditional lactyltransferase chemistry.

cited_title: Falcon/Edison Scientific ABCA4 literature research report, 2026-09-25
review_notes: Authentic research output retained unchanged as provenance. Its primary NRPE transport synthesis agrees with direct evidence, but the artifact reports the VLP ATPase rates per milligram although PMID:39222682 reports them per microgram of total VLP protein. The VLP topology and ATPase readout also require the engineered-system limits described in that primary assessment. The 2010 review is a historical transport model, not a direct transport experiment. Clinical trial and treatment summaries remain contextual and date-bound; they do not establish additional ABCA4 activities. All provider DOI and bibliography records were resolved separately.

cited_title: Identification of a fourth half ABC transporter in the human peroxisomal membrane.
review_notes: The original peroxisome claim conflicts with later full-length human ABCD4 localization and targeting evidence (PMID:19010322, PMID:27456980). The latter paper explicitly discusses the early antibody-based rat hepatic result; this is not a wrong-identifier or wrong-gene allegation.

cited_title: CGI-58, the causative gene for Chanarin-Dorfman syndrome, mediates acylation of lysophosphatidic acid.
review_notes: Identifier/title verified against primary PubMed and indexed full PMC3259832 Methods/Results. Human His-tagged protein in BL21(DE3), nickel purification, PA assays and yeast overexpression were read. Its intrinsic LPAAT interpretation is contradicted by PMID:24879803; human negative lipase/phospholipase observations and mouse WAT localization evidence remain distinct. Local cache is abstract-only.

cited_title: What are ABHD8's IBA source proteins, and does any of them justify a lipid activity?
review_notes: Source mapping is useful, but donor counts and absent target experiments do not negate an IBD. Its assertion of established ABHD5 LPAAT activity is contradicted by PMID:24879803; plant CGI-58 activities are also challenged by PMID:26745266. The intact target catalytic triad and adaptor role do not establish hydrolase loss.

cited_title: Re-expression of ABI3-binding protein suppresses thyroid tumor growth by promoting senescence and inhibiting invasion.
review_notes: Cached title matches and the paper is correctly cited; the growth-suppression result is used here and is consistent with PMID:40092729 and PMID:31174563 in other human tissues. Marked DISPUTED for the senescence claim specifically: this paper reports that gaining ABI3BP causes senescence while PMID:19338757 reports that losing it causes senescence, and three further papers report that losing it reduces senescence. The conflict is acknowledged in the field itself.

cited_title: Implication of p53-dependent cellular senescence related gene, TARSH in tumor suppression.
review_notes: Cached title matches; abstract-only; mouse embryonic fibroblasts. Correctly cited, but marked DISPUTED because its proliferation result contradicts the mouse mesenchymal stem cell knockout and knockdown data in PMID:23666637 and PMID:25296984, and its senescence direction contradicts three later knockdown studies. Used only to document the conflict; no annotation rests on it.

cited_title: ABI3BP promotes renal aging through Klotho-mediated ferroptosis.
review_notes: Cached title matches and full text is available; mouse knockout plus human HK2 cells. Correctly cited, but marked DISPUTED because its senescence direction is opposite to PMID:19338757 and PMID:18559958. Cited to document the conflict; no annotation rests on it, and neither ferroptosis nor ageing terms are proposed.

cited_title: ABI3BP deficiency alleviates Ang II-induced VSMC senescence through the Nrf2 signalling pathway.
review_notes: Cached title matches; abstract-only; mouse knockout. Correctly cited, but marked DISPUTED because the senescence direction opposes PMID:19338757 and PMID:18559958. Documents the conflict only.

cited_title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for ABRAXAS1 GO:0008017
review_notes: Provenance tracing to PTN001272083 and ABRAXAS2 is useful and agrees with the PAINT cache. The conclusion of refutation relies on primary nuclear localization, missing ABRAXAS1 assays and a single paralog source, none of which establishes loss of an ancestral function. The 2015 BRISC paper confirms the source mechanism but does not supply a direct negative ABRAXAS1 comparison.

cited_title: ACTL8: does the actin fold come with actin's residues, and do its IBA sources transfer?
review_notes: The reproducible sequence/contact calculations and fetched annotation-recipient sets are useful. Inferring a misplaced tree node from recipient membership, alignment identity or donor count is not a phylogenetic reconstruction. The ACTR3 control demonstrates that low canonical-contact conservation does not exclude all structural filament roles.

cited_title: ACTR5 controls CDKN2A and tumor progression in an INO80-independent manner.
review_notes: The only study to assay ACTR5 itself at a promoter, and the basis for the proposed GO:0000122 row. Two caveats recorded rather than hidden. It carries a 2025 erratum (PMID:41071901) correcting Fig. 2D - the CDKN2A western - because the ACTR5 and U87 panels duplicated those of Fig. 3A; the publisher states the conclusions are unaffected, and the RNA-seq, ChIP-qPCR and H3K9me2 data are independent of that panel. And the title's INO80-independence claim rests on the absence of a HepG2-selective essential domain in other subunits, while the requirement it maps runs through IES6, an INO80 subunit - so that claim is recorded in knowledge_gaps rather than annotated. Marked DISPUTED for the INO80-independence claim specifically; the CDKN2A silencing result is used.

cited_title: ADAMTSL1 and mandibular prognathism.
review_notes: The genetic association is reported without functional validation, and the proposed mechanism attributes proteolysis to a protein that has no metalloprotease domain, no catalytic activity comment and no EC number. Cited here as an example of the family-name-to-activity conflation, not as evidence for any annotation.

cited_title: ADCK1 activates the β-catenin/TCF signaling pathway to promote the growth and migration of colon cancer cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, no retraction or erratum, and the co-immunoprecipitation itself is reported at endogenous levels. Marked DISPUTED rather than MISCITED because the citation is accurate and the experiment real, but the conclusion is in tension with every localisation measurement made on this protein and has not been reproduced. Raised as a question rather than acted on.

cited_title: In vitro construction of the COQ metabolon unveils the molecular determinants of coenzyme Q biosynthesis.
review_notes: Correctly cited and methodologically substantial, but its central claim about protein kinase activity stands in direct contradiction to PMID:27499294 and UniProt records it only as "may act as a protein kinase". Included here specifically so that this review does not assert an unqualified family-level negative that the literature no longer supports.

cited_title: Adiponectin reduces thermogenesis by inhibiting brown adipose tissue activation in mice.
review_notes: Correctly cited for GO:0120163 (adiponectin suppresses thermogenesis) and incorrectly cited for the opposite term GO:0120162. The scientific claim is also genuinely disputed: PMID:26166748 reports the opposite direction in the same knockout model. Both papers are attached to both terms in GOA and in MGI.

cited_title: Adiponectin Enhances Cold-Induced Browning of Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue via Promoting M2 Macrophage Proliferation.
review_notes: Mirror image of PMID:24531262: correctly cited for GO:0120162 (adiponectin promotes cold-induced browning) and incorrectly cited for GO:0120163. Also the second independent report of the adiponectin-T-cadherin interaction, which GO records nowhere.

cited_title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ADM5 (human)
review_notes: Automated trust gates passed (accession matches C9JUS6, no non-human organism token, pairwise self-evaluation 'win'), and its nine citations are all real and correctly summarised - precision is not the problem. The problem is framing. Every functional experiment it cites is in pufferfish, medaka, Xenopus, pig, rat or sheep, yet the narrative is written as a description of the human gene and never mentions that the human mature peptide is deleted, even though its own 2006 dated finding records the anthropoid deletion. Taken at face value this record would have produced eight ACCEPTs. Marked DISPUTED for that reason: correctly cited, but the claim it advances about this gene is contested by UniProt and by the sequence. Used here for literature discovery only.

cited_title: The structure of human ADP-ribosylhydrolase 3 (ARH3) provides insights into the reversibility of protein ADP-ribosylation.
review_notes: The 1.6 A ARH3 structure, and the source of the micromolar ADP-ribose binding measurement. Its statement that ARH3 'efficiently de-ADP-ribosylates poly- but not monoADP-ribosylated proteins' was superseded in 2017: ARH3 is the serine mono-ADP-ribosylhydrolase. The 2006 assay used arginine-linked mono-ADP-ribose, on which ARH3 is genuinely inactive, so the two results are compatible once the substrate is specified. Marked DISPUTED so the older negative is not re-imported.

cited_title: SUZ12 is required for both the histone methyltransferase activity and the silencing function of the EED-EZH2 complex.
review_notes: Source of the long-standing view that AEBP2 stimulates PRC2, reported here as a minimal complex of EZH2, EED and SUZ12 with AEBP2 required for optimal activity. PMID:41168462 reports that prior in vitro stimulation was obtained with the short isoform or with N-terminally truncated constructs, and that the broadly expressed long isoform inhibits instead. Marked DISPUTED for the direction of the effect, not for the citation: the disagreement is genuine and in the literature, and the cached record is abstract-only so the construct used cannot be determined from it.

cited_title: Distinct Stimulatory Mechanisms Regulate the Catalytic Activity of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2.
review_notes: Reports that AEBP2 stimulates both PRC2-EZH1 and PRC2-EZH2 by a mechanism independent of and additive to allosteric activation. Like PMID:15225548 this is disputed in direction by PMID:41168462, which attributes prior stimulation results to use of the short isoform or of N-terminally truncated protein. Cited here for the mechanism it describes, not as support for a stimulatory annotation.

cited_title: The mixed-lineage leukemia fusion partner AF4 stimulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation and mediates coordinated chromatin remodeling.
review_notes: PubMed-verified, and cited here ONLY for what it actually shows: a mouse Af4 result. It carries an unflagged 2023 Erratum (PMID:37777189), and its DOT1L-recruitment claim rests on an ENL co-immunoprecipitate that PMID:20159561 reports was misinterpreted. Nothing in this review asserts DOT1L recruitment by AFF1.

cited_title: AFF1 and AFF4 differentially regulate the osteogenic differentiation of human MSCs.
review_notes: PubMed-verified. Carries an unflagged 2020 Correction (PMID:32257529) whose content is not stated in its abstract or its PMC record, and one sentence in the overexpression section says "AFF1-depleted" where the figure describes overexpressing cells; both are recorded in the notes and the claims used avoid that sentence. LOW_QUALITY is not the right flag - the experiments are sound and bidirectional - but the correction is unresolved.

cited_title: Role of HRB in clathrin-dependent endocytosis.
review_notes: Supports the clathrin-dependent-endocytosis role by knockdown, and is one of only two papers the affinage record returned. Marked DISPUTED because its generality is contested rather than because the paper is unsound: it reports transferrin uptake strongly reduced on HRB knockdown, while PMID:18775314 reports no effect of HRB depletion on EGF internalisation or degradation and reads AGFG1 as a SNARE-specific adaptor. Both results are recorded; this review does not adjudicate between them. The cache's Full Text section holds only page boilerplate, so only the abstract is used.

cited_title: Organization patterns of the AGFG genes: an evolutionary study.
review_notes: The mammals-only claim conflicts with the broader AGFG phylogeny in PMID:23433073. This is a claim-specific disagreement, not a judgment that the entire study is low quality; the sequence-symbol census is corroboration rather than an orthology proof.

cited_title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AGFG2 (human)
review_notes: Full body and table read. Useful dual Nef/Vpu narrative agrees with primary evidence. The table contradicts that narrative, detailed binding/localization is partly extrapolated from Hrb, the mammals-only statement conflicts with broader phylogeny, and the report omits the endothelial secretion study.

cited_title: Identification of an angiogenic factor that when mutated causes susceptibility to Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
review_notes: The source of seven of AGGF1's twenty-four GOA rows, and the biochemistry it reports - secretion, endothelial binding, CAM angiogenesis, proliferation, TWEAK interaction - has been independently reproduced and extended. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED for one specific reason: its human-genetic claim, that E133K is a gain-of-function KTS mutation, was contradicted by PMID:16443853 and PMID:17103452 and effectively withdrawn by the originating laboratory in PMID:18564129, and ClinVar now classifies the variant Benign/Likely benign. None of the GO rows sourced from this paper depends on that claim, which is why they are all accepted.

cited_title: Protein therapy of skeletal muscle atrophy and mechanism by angiogenic factor AGGF1.
review_notes: Not disputed as a citation - the paper says what it says - but its central mechanistic claim is contradicted in direction by PMID:39905000. Recording both, and annotating neither, is the honest treatment. No quote is taken from it.

cited_title: UniProt record for human AGK
review_notes: Identity, reactions, domains and localization checked. The C6-ceramide reaction RHEA:43312 is attributed to PMID:15939762, which instead reports a negative assay for C6-ceramide. The separate general ceramide reaction is an ortholog inference. Positive MAG/DAG and TIM22 information is supported independently; do not silently edit the machine record.

cited_title: OpenScientist hypothesis report for AGK ceramide kinase activity
review_notes: Read and reused the existing report. Its human ceramide-kinase conclusion is supported by direct negative substrate assays. However, the report incorrectly presents the PAINT assertion as CERK-to-AGK propagation: PTN008994514 is supported by mouse Agk and fly Mulk. It also does not independently resolve ceramide/sphingosine biosynthetic-process annotations. Retain the biochemical observations and exact report excerpt while rejecting those overextended phylogenetic/pathway explanations. The report also says Bektas did not mention ceramide and describes limited human testing; the cached human Results explicitly tested it. Therefore primary assay text supplies the revised supporting quotes.

cited_title: Let-7a-regulated translational readthrough of mammalian AGO1 generates a microRNA pathway inhibitor.
review_notes: The original readthrough and AGO1x inhibitory-function study is directly challenged by PMID:40500330 and defended in PMID:40500329. The latter response was verified from PubMed and the publisher full text. Reporter-method disagreement does not by itself invalidate orthogonal proteomic/antibody evidence or all proteoform functions. No seeded GOA row cites this paper.

cited_title: Transcript-specific induction of stop codon readthrough using a CRISPR-dCas13 system.
review_notes: Full cached dCas13 readthrough-induction study uses AGO1 reporters and endogenous-protein assays. Its reporter interpretation is challenged in PMID:40500330 and defended in PMID:40500329. The criticism is scoped to readthrough measurement, not assumed to refute every dCas13 result or AGO1 function.

cited_title: The dual luciferase assay does not support claims of stop codon readthrough on the AGO1 mRNA.
review_notes: The full cached methodological critique shows low signal in its insulated reporter and attributes earlier values to reporter effects. Its interpretation is explicitly contested by the co-published response PMID:40500329, which discusses reporter design and orthogonal evidence. This is an unresolved experimental disagreement, not a retraction. The earlier claim that no response existed is superseded.

cited_title: Response to Suresh et al.
review_notes: PubMed independently verified the identifier, title and DOI 10.1038/s44318-025-00479-0; publisher full text was read. The normal fetch artifact recovered on 2026-09-27 now supplies XML full text from PMC12264181. The authors contest the critique using prior AGO1 reporter and orthogonal evidence and new HBB reporter comparisons with versus without stop-go sequences. The HBB experiment is not itself an endogenous AGO1 abundance measurement. This reply and the methodological critique leave the endogenous readthrough dispute unresolved; DISPUTED remains the appropriate scientific assessment despite verified identity and recovered access.

cited_title: An mRNA m7G cap binding-like motif within human Ago2 represses translation.
review_notes: Identifier/title checked against the machine-cached primary record and original GOA citation; access scope is stated below. PubMed confirms the paper proposing a MID-domain cap-binding motif and cap-dependent repression. Direct cap recognition is contested by structural and recombinant-protein studies (PMID:19159466 and PMID:21475248); PMID:23409027 supplies later cap-proximity evidence in cellular complexes. The reference is DISPUTED specifically for intrinsic cap binding, not for every reported guide-binding, slicing or repression result. The cached record is abstract-only.

cited_title: Cancer exosomes perform cell-independent microRNA biogenesis and promote tumorigenesis.
review_notes: Identifier/title checked against the machine-cached primary record and original GOA citation; access scope is stated below. PubMed links this original to the 2025 Expression of Concern PMID:40930611, DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2025.07.022. The full notice was read at the MD Anderson ElsevierPure institutional record on 2026-09-27. It reports an institutional investigation of duplicated/relabelled Dicer, CD9, tRNA, miRNA, flotillin and TSG101 panels and a recommendation for retraction, disputed by some authors, with journal review ongoing. This is an Expression of Concern, not a retraction or proof that a particular AGO2 pair is false. Independent exosomal AGO2 evidence is assessed separately.

cited_title: OpenScientist AGO4 mRNA destabilization versus slicer-loss adjudication
review_notes: Read complete report and CSV tables. Useful PMID:19838187 tethering evidence independently verified. Material error: report asserts no GO:0035279/GO:0090625 negative annotations, but live QuickGO retains both BHF-UCL NOT IDA rows. Definitions of both terms explicitly concern cleavage; related deadenylation synonyms for GO:0035279 do not automatically broaden its formal definition. Reject confident removal/re-scoping of source NOT based on names or presumed annotation absence; retain uncertainty and request ontology/assay clarification.

cited_title: Linkage analysis and whole exome sequencing reveals AHNAK2 as a novel genetic cause for autosomal recessive CMT in a Malaysian family.
review_notes: The genetic finding is sound and correctly cited. The disputed element is the background claim that AHNAK2 binds directly to periaxin: a Europe PMC search for AHNAK2 and periaxin returns nothing earlier than PMID:24675079, which reports domain-swapped homodimers of each protein separately rather than a heterodimer. No annotation in this review rests on the interaction claim; it is raised in suggested_questions instead. Separately, the affinage record describes these as compound heterozygous variants, whereas the abstract describes a consanguineous autosomal recessive family - not load-bearing, but noted.

cited_title: AIRE functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
review_notes: Primary PMC Methods/Results and newly recovered full text inspected. Human AIRE cDNA supplies GST-PHD and full-length preparations; E1/E2/ubiquitin assays with GST/PHD2 controls report positive E3 activity. This is real experimental evidence, not only domain projection. PMID:15649886 reports failure to reproduce intrinsic PHD1 E3 activity/E2 interaction; retain the conflict without inventing contamination. Source4 recovered full text, but does not resolve the disagreement between assay preparations.

cited_title: Automatic transfer of experimentally verified manual GO annotation data to orthologs using Ensembl Compara
review_notes: The orthology itself is sound - Q5QD51 is reviewed rat Akap12 in the same single-gene PANTHER subfamily as human AKAP12, so these are ortholog and not paralog transfers. The donor annotations are mixed in quality, and the pipeline propagates them without distinction: three of the eleven transferred rows rest on expression correlation or, in the GO:0043116 case, invert the sign of the experiment they cite. Marked DISPUTED for that reason rather than for any identifier problem.

cited_title: Research Report: Human AKIRIN1 (UniProt Q9H9L7; Akirin-1/Mighty) — functional annotation
review_notes: Full biological report and evidence-table artifact read. Useful promyogenic synthesis and explicit Akirin1 versus Akirin2 immune distinction. Positive proliferation is condition-specific, and the fibroblast perturbation species was checked in the primary paper. Association studies are not additional process evidence.

cited_title: ZNRF2 is released from membranes by growth factors and, together with ZNRF1, regulates the Na+/K+ATPase.
review_notes: Source identity was checked against its seeded IDA citation and the cached primary record. Full original PMC3500867 maps PKBalpha phosphorylation to ZNRF2 Ser19 by HPLC/Edman sequencing (supplementary Figure S2A). Publisher note DOI:10.1242/jcs.259936 reports duplicated bottom GST control blots in Figure 2B and unavailable original LICOR controls; alternate same-experiment controls were oversaturated. The mapped serine chemistry is retained with this explicit figure-integrity limitation, not converted into evidence for Tyr catalysis. The local cache is abstract-only or metadata-only; external full-text access, when obtained, is identified above.

cited_title: AKT can phosphorylate NR4A1 (NUR77)
review_notes: The live Reactome event summary, participants and catalyst assignment were read at https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-199863. The event models nuclear AKT phosphorylation of NR4A1 but explicitly notes subsequent work favoring RSK/MSK as the physiological NR4A1 kinase. The physiological NR4A1-kinase assignment is disputed in the wild-type event; the general AKT kinase and nuclear-location assertions remain separately supported.

cited_title: AKT1 E17K mutant phosphorylates NR4A1 (NUR77)
review_notes: The live Reactome event summary, participants and catalyst assignment were read at https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-2399988. The event predicts nuclear AKT1 E17K phosphorylation of NR4A1; its wild-type counterpart also records uncertainty about the physiological NR4A1 kinase. The physiological NR4A1-kinase assignment is disputed in the wild-type event; the general AKT kinase and nuclear-location assertions remain separately supported.

cited_title: AKTIP noncatalytic K63 ubiquitination and lesion bypass: focused OpenScientist report
review_notes: Read the full report, citation index, and HTML/PDF report artifacts. Correctly distinguishes missing E2 catalytic cysteine and telomere-replication assays from lesion-bypass assays. Its proposed process refutation is not established: actual PAINT descent includes PTN000630262, experimentally seeded by UBE2N and orthologs, and its negative assertions are on other branches. Pairwise sequence identities, a distinct CDD model and missing IntAct partners do not demonstrate process loss. The artifacts contain rendered reports, not alignment code or raw interaction outputs. Independent PMID:36516775 supports a noncatalytic ubiquitination-related context but neither specifies K63 linkage nor proves the proposed CUL2 activity mechanism.

cited_title: Heme Scavenging and Delivery: The Role of Human Serum Albumin.
review_notes: Identifier and full narrative-review text verified. The disputed point is its introductory claim that heme is part of cyanocobalamin; ChEBI identifies cyanocobalamin as a cobalt-centered corrin. This bounded error is not used to reject albumin heme binding, which is independently supported by the original human-albumin transfer experiment. The seeded EXP code remains unchanged, but the review is not treated as a new direct assay. Unrelated speculative assertions are not adopted.

cited_title: Precision diagnosis and treatment of vitamin metabolism-related epilepsy.
review_notes: Primary PubMed DOI/identifier mapping is verified; full cached clinical review and its ALDH7A1 section were read. The ALDH7A1 subsection switches to ALDH4A1 in its treatment paragraph and uses inconsistent metabolite names, including piperonylic acid in the lysine-pathway caption. These secondary-source wording problems are not adopted as target mechanism. The section is useful clinical context, but proposed glial/neurogenesis roles and broad therapeutic claims are not new experiments. DISPUTED is limited to the identified mechanistic/gene-attribution wording, not the identifier or all disease observations.

cited_title: ALK binds ligand pleiotrophin (PTN)
review_notes: Actual normal-fetched record and complete summary read. This legacy model describes direct PTN binding. PMID:17681947 instead demonstrates an indirect PTN–PTPRZ route, and the ALKAL studies establish direct cytokine ligands. The model title does not settle direct PTN binding. The summary is a pathway model, not a new direct experiment; cited literature inside it was not automatically claimed as individually read.

cited_title: ALK binds ligand midkine (MDK)
review_notes: Actual normal-fetched record and complete summary read. Direct MDK binding is a historical model whose physiological ligand interpretation is less secure than the ALKAL evidence; the localization assertion does not establish the ligand mechanism. The summary is a pathway model, not a new direct experiment; cited literature inside it was not automatically claimed as individually read.

cited_title: DNA methylation on N(6)-adenine in mammalian embryonic stem cells.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Wu et al., Nature 2016). The mouse ESC precedent for Alkbh1 as a 6mA eraser. Included because it is the origin of the eraser hypothesis; its central claim about mammalian genomic 6mA abundance is directly contested by PMID:32206710, PMID:32203414 and PMID:35113693.

cited_title: N(6)-Methyladenine DNA Modification in the Human Genome.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Xiao et al., Mol Cell 2018). Only the abstract is cached. This is one of the two EXP sources for GO:0141131. Its central premise - that 6mA is extensively present in the human genome - is contested by PMID:32206710, PMID:32203414, PMID:35113693 and PMID:41254163. Retained and cited, with the dispute recorded rather than the annotation removed.

cited_title: N(6)-methyladenine DNA Modification in Glioblastoma.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Xie et al., Cell 2018). The second EXP source for GO:0141131. Same dispute as PMID:30017583; the glioblastoma 6mA mapping relies on antibody-based detection, which is the specific technique challenged by PMID:32206710.

cited_title: YTHDF3 recognizes DNA N6-methyladenine and recruits ALKBH1 for 6mA removal from genomic DNA.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Chen et al., EMBO J 2025). Full text cached. Proposes YTHDF3 as the reader that enables ALKBH1 to act on duplex genomic 6mA. Cited here chiefly because its own abstract concedes that ALKBH1 does not demethylate 6mA in dsDNA and that the genomic activity remains largely debated. Senior authorship overlaps with PMID:30017583, so it is a continuation of the same programme rather than independent confirmation.

cited_title: Pathogenesis of Cardiomyopathy Caused by Variants in ALPK3, an Essential Pseudokinase in the Cardiomyocyte Nucleus and Sarcomere.
review_notes: Primary identifier and DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.122.059688 verified. Full PMC Methods, Results and Figures 2-6 read. Human isogenic cardiomyocytes, mouse knockout and human tissue show myomesin mislocalization and sarcomere disruption. Tagged ALPK3 in human cardiomyocytes localizes to M bands and nuclear envelope; HEK293T co-IP supports MYOM2 association, while MYOM1 co-IP was negative despite colocalization. Cellular catalytic-cleft mutations and overexpression support the pseudokinase interpretation, but do not establish absence of catalysis under every biochemical condition. PMID:39196058 reports a conflicting positive domain assay. Historical residue numbers use the article sequence rather than current 1705-aa UniProt coordinates. Primary access route: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9698156/ . The normal publication record is now cached and its actual contents were independently read. Actual extracted Methods, relevant Results/Figures and Discussion read: isogenic human hiPSC-CMs with truncations, G1777E/D1784A dual-cleft and D1774A single-cleft variants; cellular phosphoproteomics and HEK293T overexpression support a noncatalytic model within those conditions. Tagged ALPK3 is at M-bands and predominantly nuclear envelope in these models; endogenous antibody specificity is problematic. MYOM2 co-IP is positive in HEK293T, while MYOM1 co-IP is negative despite colocalization. Mouse knockout supplies separate in-vivo structural evidence. Cellular negative phosphoproteomics does not universally disprove a biochemical activity under other conditions.

cited_title: ALPK3 Functions as a Pseudokinase.
review_notes: Primary identifier and DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.123.065993 verified. Full PMC research letter and Figure 1 read. Recombinant mouse ALPK3 residues 1339-1608 fail to phosphorylate heat-inactivated rat H9c2 or human cardiomyocyte lysates containing SQSTM1; mouse TRPM7 is a positive control. Mouse K1420R knock-in retains cardiac function and SQSTM1 phosphosignal. These negative results are substantive but concern a mouse isolated domain and a mouse mutation, rather than every full-length human context. They conflict with PMID:39196058; neither a proven contaminant nor universal inactivity is asserted. Primary access route: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10697696/ . The normal publication record is now cached and its actual contents were independently read. Entire actual experimental research-letter body and Figure 1 caption read, despite its short format/no PubMed abstract: murine ALPK3 domain 1339–1608, murine TRPM7 positive control, heat-inactivated rat H9c2/human hiPSC-CM lysates and radiolabeled ATP; no ALPK3 activity under tested conditions. Mouse K1420R preserves adult cardiac function and SQSTM1 T269/S272 ratio. Modeled nucleotide pockets are not measured binding. This is real negative evidence, not a universal inactivity proof.

cited_title: Alpha kinase 3 signaling at the M-band maintains sarcomere integrity and proteostasis in striated muscle.
review_notes: Primary identifier and DOI 10.1038/s44161-023-00219-9 verified. Full PMC Methods, Results and Extended Data Figure 9 read. Endogenous tagged human ALPK3, human cardiac organoids and a mouse truncation model support M-band organization. Bacterially expressed His-tagged ALPK3 domain, reported residues 1577-1828, increases lysate phosphopeptides after irreversible endogenous-kinase inhibition. The SQSTM1-HA assay uses HEK293FT immunoprecipitates, active versus heat-denatured domain and phosphatase controls; it is not a wholly purified two-protein reaction. Positive phosphorylation evidence is retained, while intrinsic activity and the combined T269/S272 readout remain unresolved against PMID:38048395. Neither host-cell species nor old residue numbering is silently equated to a current canonical construct. Primary access route: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11358020/ . The normal publication record is now cached and its actual contents were independently read. Actual Methods, relevant Results/Figures and Discussion read: human tagged hPSC cardiomyocytes and mouse W1538X models; live tagged localization supports M-band and lacks a detected nuclear signal in that model. Recombinant domain 1577–1828 is expressed in E. coli BL21 and Ni-NTA purified. CM lysates are treated with fluorosulfonylbenzoyladenosine and dialyzed before addition of recombinant domain versus water. The targeted assay uses SQSTM1-HA immunoprecipitated from HEK293FT, active versus heat-denatured domain and lambda-phosphatase controls. These are positive kinase results that must be retained; the target is not a purified two-protein system and T269/S272 antibody does not isolate the residue class. Recombinant-domain species is not assigned merely from the bacterial or human host. Cellular proteomic changes include downstream effects.

cited_title: Deep research report: human ALPL / tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP)
review_notes: Genuine pre-existing Falcon/Edison report and its artifact are preserved unchanged. It is secondary research output, not a primary experiment. Its DOI bibliography has been independently resolved to eight real publications, including seven currently missing caches. The blanket mouse-only characterization of phosphocreatine chemistry is too coarse: PMID:33981039 directly assays recombinant human TNAP, while mouse targeting/physiology remains distinct. No provider report was fabricated when the new Falcon/fallback attempt failed.

cited_title: ALS2/Alsin regulates Rac-PAK signaling and neurite outgrowth.
review_notes: Official PubMed identity and original author-uploaded JBC full article verified. Methods uses human full-length ALS2, human-brain/KIAA1563 cDNA, CHO Rac-GTP capture/PAK1 kinase assays and rat E18 neuronal outgrowth. The positive cellular results stand; direct Rac-GEF interpretation is contested by PMID:17409386, which instead places ALS2 downstream of active Rac1. There is no direct ALS2–PAK1 binding or GTP-hydrolysis assay in the inspected Methods/Results. Local cache remains abstract-only.

cited_title: Alsin is a Rab5 and Rac1 guanine nucleotide exchange factor.
review_notes: Official PubMed title/DOI verified (10.1074/jbc.M313504200). Original full PDF read at https://mcm.h-its.org/mcm/projects/rab/literature/Alsin.pdf. Human cDNA from SH-SY5Y/KIAA1563, bacterial VPS9 constructs and GDP-release assays support direct Rab5 exchange; human ALS2 in NIH3T3 provides construct-level localization, whereas endogenous neuronal staining is rat. Rac activation is measured by GTP-state capture after Sf9 coexpression, not purified Rac GDP release. PMID:17409386 disputes the direct Rac-GEF interpretation without negating Rab5 catalysis or the original positive cell assay. The recovered normal publication record is abstract-only and its complete actual abstract was read. Prior external full-text access, where documented above, remains separate; recovery does not imply that Methods, figures or supplements are present in this cache.

cited_title: BLOC-1 complex deficiency alters the targeting of adaptor protein complex-3 cargoes.
review_notes: Sound cell biology - AP-3 and BLOC-1 on shared small vesicles, and mistargeting of LAMP1, PI4KIIalpha and VAMP7-TI. What is disputed is the GO term derived from it: the paper's 'microvesicles' are intracellular transport intermediates, whereas GO:1990742 denotes an extracellular vesicle shed from the plasma membrane.

cited_title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: Correctly cited for AP-3 binding clathrin, and the binding is real, but its functional inference ('AP-3 function in protein sorting may depend on clathrin') has been superseded: PMID:23761069 shows the association is dispensable and PMID:42139345 shows AP3:ARF1 builds carriers with no clathrin lattice. Also note the interaction it maps is beta3's appendage, not delta's.

cited_title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: The in vitro clathrin-binding result behind the NAS GO:0035654 row. Correctly cited and a real experiment, but its central claim is contested: the interaction is with beta3 rather than mu3A, the authors' own conclusion is hedged ('may depend on clathrin'), the 2024 review of the field calls the question open, and the 2026 reconstitution shows carrier formation without a clathrin lattice. DISPUTED rather than MISCITED - the paper says what the annotation says it says.

cited_title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for AP3M2 (human)
review_notes: Read all six cited findings. Useful neuronal/pigment-cell context, but calling AP3M2 mu-2 is inaccurate (mu3B); zebrafish and mouse findings are not direct human assays. It does not settle clathrin or TGN questions.

cited_title: Association of the AP-3 adaptor complex with clathrin.
review_notes: Correctly cited, and its in vitro finding that the beta-3 appendage binds the clathrin heavy chain is not in question. The conclusion built on it - that AP-3 function involves clathrin coats - has been contested by direct reconstitution and coat tomography [PMID:42139345], which is why the annotation it supports is modified to a coat-agnostic term rather than accepted as written. Flagged DISPUTED for the downstream claim, not for the citation.

cited_title: Characterization of MUDENG, a novel anti-apoptotic protein.
review_notes: Full text cached. Reports the opposite sign to PMID:18395520 and PMID:31427081, with MuD depletion sensitising astroglioma cells to TRAIL. Its endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial localisation rests on a crude microsomal preparation made with a commercial ER isolation kit, a fraction that co-purifies endosomes and lysosomes, so it is not resolution enough to contradict the endolysosomal localisation and no ER or mitochondrion term is proposed from it.

cited_title: Pathological alpha-synuclein transmission initiated by binding lymphocyte-activation gene 3.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Science 2016). Background for the receptor field rather than direct APLP1 evidence. The central LAG3 claim was subsequently contested by PMID:34309222.

cited_title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The UniProt subcellular-location mapping itself operates correctly; what it maps is unreliable for this protein. One of the four rows it generates (mitochondrial inner membrane) is accepted; the other three (Secreted, Golgi apparatus membrane, endoplasmic reticulum membrane) are removed because the UniProt statements behind them rest on a protein species PMID:37279200 showed is not MIC26. Flagged DISPUTED rather than MISCITED because the defect is in the upstream UniProt record, not in this GO_REF's procedure, and it will resolve when that record is updated.

cited_title: ApoO, a novel apolipoprotein, is an original glycoprotein up-regulated by diabetes in human heart.
review_notes: The paper that named APOO, and the origin of every secretory annotation on this gene. Correctly cited and historically important, but its central protein assignment has been overturned: the 55 kDa immunoreactive species on which the secretion, glycosylation, lipoprotein-association and cholesterol-efflux observations all rest is unchanged by MIC26 knockdown and knockout and contains no MIC26 peptides (PMID:37279200). Cached abstract only; the GOA EXP annotation on it is nevertheless removed here, because the refutation is a direct, knockout-controlled re-examination of that exact band and not an inference from the abstract.

cited_title: The non-glycosylated isoform of MIC26 is a constituent of the mammalian MICOS complex and promotes formation of crista junctions.
review_notes: The single most heavily used reference on this gene, supplying nine GOA rows. Its mitochondrial conclusions - inner-membrane MIC26 as a MICOS subunit interacting with MIC60, MIC27 and MIC10, and required for crista junction number - are accepted in full. Its three-form model is not: the glycosylated/secreted 55 kDa species and its ER/Golgi precursor were withdrawn by the same laboratory in PMID:37279200 (Anand and Reichert are authors of both). Hence its nine rows split three ACCEPT, three MODIFY and three REMOVE. Cached abstract only, but the refutation is explicit and author-confirmed.

cited_title: UniProtKB entry Q9BUR5 (MIC26_HUMAN)
review_notes: The fetched Q9BUR5 record; accession asserted to be the expected protein (MIC26_HUMAN, 198 aa), not a merged accession resolving elsewhere. Its function, subunit and mitochondrial inner-membrane sections are current and correct. Three things in it are stale: the Secreted / Golgi apparatus membrane / endoplasmic reticulum membrane locations and the chondroitin-sulfate PTM line, all traceable to the species refuted in PMID:37279200; and SIGNAL 1..25 (ECO:0000255, prediction only) where the paralogue Q6UXV4 carries TRANSIT 1..27. The mouse orthologue's record Q9DCZ4 already lists only the inner membrane.

cited_title: Gene Ontology annotation through association of InterPro records with GO terms
review_notes: The pipeline itself is sound and correctly applied: ARFGEF3 genuinely carries InterPro IPR000904 (Sec7 domain). What is disputed is the inference the mapping encodes for this entry, namely that presence of the Sec7 domain implies exchange factor activity. ARFGEF3's Sec7 domain has lost the catalytic glutamate, so both GO terms this reference supplies (GO:0005085 and GO:0032012) overstate what the domain can do here. Recorded as DISPUTED rather than MISCITED because the defect is in a domain-to-activity rule, not in the citation.

cited_title: Gene Ontology annotation based on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot Subcellular Location vocabulary mapping, accompanied by conservative changes to GO terms applied by UniProt
review_notes: The SL-0086 (Cytoplasm) mapping is exact. The SL-0244 and SL-0245 mappings are not: UniProt's own definition of SL-0244 describes regulated exocytosis of hormones and neurotransmitters, but the mapping sends it to GO:0030133 transport vesicle, which GO defines as the constitutive secretory pathway. GO:0030141 secretory granule and GO:0030133 are disjoint sibling branches under GO:0031410, verified against QuickGO's is_a/part_of closure, so this is a wrong-branch mapping rather than a coarse one. Affects the vocabulary rule, not this gene alone.

cited_title: Affinage mechanistic annotation for ARHGAP36 (human)
review_notes: Full report reviewed. Its PKA, GLI and entosis narrative provides useful primary leads; its broad catalytic/transcription-regulator GO grounding is not direct evidence that ARHGAP36 catalyzes a protein reaction or acts at DNA. Coverage omissions and a provider self-score alone do not establish low scientific quality. Primary structural, catalytic-screen and new accessible entosis data determine the judgments.

cited_title: Inhibitory effects of Arhgap6 on cervical carcinoma cells.
review_notes: Cited by Reactome R-HSA-9018806 as establishing RAC3-directed GAP activity for ARHGAP6. The paper itself reports a co-immunoprecipitation between Arhgap6 and Rac3 and never measures GTPase activity, so the GAP-activity reading is not supported by it. The paper is correctly cited as a Rac3 interaction; what is disputed is the inference drawn from it.

cited_title: RAC3 GAPs stimulate RAC3 GTPase activity
review_notes: Places ARHGAP6 in the tier of GAPs shown to stimulate RAC3 GTPase activity, citing only PMID:26628301, which shows binding and not catalysis. The GO term it produces is still true of ARHGAP6 for a different substrate, so the row is kept; the pathway assertion behind it is what is disputed.

cited_title: The HPV16 E6 binding protein Tip-1 interacts with ARHGEF16, which activates Cdc42.
review_notes: Correctly cited and the source of four GO rows, including the TAX1BP3 PDZ interaction which is sound. Marked DISPUTED for its Cdc42 arm alone: PMID:20679435 reports no cellular Cdc42 activation and no binding to nucleotide-free Cdc42 in HEK293T cells, with Zizimin1 as positive control. The two reconcile if Cdc42 activation is conditional on Tip-1 and HPV16 E6, which is how this review treats it. Separately, the GO:0005096 molecular function drawn from this paper is a term-choice error on GOA's side, not a defect of the paper, which calls ARHGEF16 a GEF throughout. Abstract-only in the cache.

cited_title: p75NTR indirectly activates RAC and Cdc42 via a guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor
review_notes: Source of one cytosol TAS row. DISPUTED rather than MISCITED, because the claim GOA actually draws from this reaction is GO:0005829 cytosol and that claim is correctly supported; what is contested is the reaction's own set-level GTPase output, which never reaches GOA. ARHGEF16 is one of 52 protein participants in a set-level GEF catalyst whose asserted outputs are Rac and Cdc42 - both of which PMID:20679435 specifically failed to detect for Ephexin4 in cells, with Dock180 and Zizimin1 as positive controls.

cited_title: GEFs activate RhoA,B,C
review_notes: Source of the other cytosol TAS row, and DISPUTED for the same reason as R-HSA-205039: the cytosol claim it supports is fine, the substrate claim it makes is contested and never reaches GOA. The catalyst is a 54-participant DefinedSet of Dbl-family GEFs assembled by domain rather than by measured specificity - it contains TIAM1 and TIAM2 (Rac-only), FGD1-FGD4 and ITSN1 (Cdc42-only), SOS1, SOS2 and RASGRF2 (Ras), and all five ephexins - and its output is RHOA/B/C:GTP. PMID:20679435 could not detect RhoA activation by Ephexin4.

cited_title: G Protein betagamma subunits stimulate p114RhoGEF, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for RhoA and Rac1: regulation of cell shape and reactive oxygen species production.
review_notes: Correctly cited and it is the source of the gene's only curated molecular-function annotation, but its Rac1 conclusion is contradicted by the purified-protein experiment in PMID:11085924 and by the depletion experiment in PMID:21258369. Marked DISPUTED for that reason, not for any citation defect. No free full text was found, so the assessment rests on the abstract plus the two contradicting papers.

cited_title: WGEF is a novel RhoGEF expressed in intestine, liver, heart, and kidney.
review_notes: PubMed-verified as Wang et al., Biochem Biophys Res Commun 324:1053-8 (2004), and independently corroborated as the ARHGEF19 evidence cited by Reactome R-HSA-8980691. Marked DISPUTED rather than VERIFIED because its substrate claim is contradicted by the later side-by-side retest in PMID:18256687, not because the citation is wrong. Cached as abstract only; the full text was not consulted.

cited_title: Dishevelled2 activates WGEF via its interaction with a unique internal peptide motif of the GEF.
review_notes: Important and carefully done, but it contradicts PMID:18256687 on where Dishevelled binds and neither mapping has been reproduced independently, so DISPUTED records a live disagreement rather than a fault. Two things a reader of the database rather than the paper would get wrong: the activity measurements are on Xenopus protein, and PDB 8YR7 - which UniProt lists under Q8IW93, implying a human ARHGEF19 structure - is the failed fusion, with the WGEF peptide not usefully resolved. The residue claims were checked against the current UniProt sequence: position 295 is Y and residues 349-359 read GSTFSLWQDIP. PubMed- and PMC-verified (PMC11076555); full text cached and read.

cited_title: ATP13A1 Dislocase Hypothesis: Final Report
review_notes: Substantive productive-topogenesis finding is supported by primary studies. The 2026 Spf1 experiment measures substrate-stimulated ATP hydrolysis, not a complete purified dislocation cycle; calcium-homeostasis review flag does not establish loss of a process role.

cited_title: Falcon deep research report for human ATP7B
review_notes: Immutable provider report retained as a research record. Its cell-only interpretation of copper import and blanket mitochondrial exclusion are superseded by official GO definitions and primary evidence documented in the manual notes. It is not used as the sole support for the transport core.

cited_title: OpenScientist focused report on BAIAP2L2/Pinkbar nucleoplasm localization
review_notes: The report adds a current-database absence check and summarizes direct membrane/vesicle/stereocilia localization. Its own limitations admit that missing nuclear annotations, null HPA fields and a heuristic NLS scan do not exclude a nuclear pool; these data do not justify the stronger refuted verdict. The historical GOA source is known (PTN001022094), although absent from the current cache. Its suggested clathrin cross-organism misattribution is contradicted by the PMID:21401524 abstract, which explicitly tests human BAIAP2L2.

cited_title: BRCA1 supports XIST RNA concentration on the inactive X chromosome.
review_notes: PubMed identity and complete original abstract verified (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12419249/). The broader claim that BRCA1 directly controls XIST localization was challenged by the primary study at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17146760/; its complete abstract was read, not its full Methods. This dispute concerns the BRCA1-dependent localization model, not a demonstrated refutation of the original BARD1-associated RNA observation. The original selected anti-BARD1 immunoprecipitation Results were read in the initial review; direct versus indirect RNA binding remains unresolved. Retain the existing BARD1 RNA-binding annotation as non-core.

cited_title: Direct role of Bardet-Biedl syndrome proteins in transcriptional regulation.
review_notes: Primarily BBS7-centric; shows BBS7 interaction with PcG member RNF2 (Q99496) and proposes a nuclear/transcriptional role for BBS proteins generally. The transcriptional role for BBS2 specifically is indirect and contested versus the well-established cytoplasmic/ciliary trafficking function.

cited_title: Direct role of Bardet-Biedl syndrome proteins in transcriptional regulation.
review_notes: Primarily a BBS7 study (nuclear role, RNF2/PcG interaction); BBS4-specific transcription-factor-binding is a weak generalization and is treated as an over-annotation here.

cited_title: PPM1K dephosphorylates p-BCKDH
review_notes: Complete normal human Reactome frontmatter and short summary read in the verified archive, then matched byte-for-byte to the canonical import. This cache contains no explicit compartment, participant or catalyst-entity fields; cited primary papers and pathway graphs were not newly reviewed through this recovery. The normal summary calls the dephosphorylated target E1 beta. This conflicts with the alpha phosphorylation loop characterized in PMID:15166214 and PMID:15576032 and the reviewed alpha-chain UniProt record. Flag that subunit wording as disputed while preserving the machine source unchanged. PPM1K supplies phosphatase activity; neither E1 chain is a phosphatase. The discrepancy does not refute the independently supported matrix localization.

cited_title: BCL2 conditional proapoptotic and channel capacities: focused OpenScientist report
review_notes: The complete report supports retaining conditional proapoptotic and intrinsic channel capacities, consistent with the independently checked primary texts. Its acidic-pH-only permeabilization summary must be restricted to the carboxyfluorescein assay in PMID:9219694: PMID:9144199 directly records neutral-pH ion channels. The report admits that it did not inspect actual PAINT nodes and reviewed no mouse functional primary assays. It does not resolve oligomeric pore-complex membership; no duplicate NEW annotations are adopted.

cited_title: Phospho-R-Smad1/5/8 dissociates from the receptor complex
review_notes: Internal title/body mismatch in the cached Reactome record; this flags source specificity, not a retraction or evidence against BMPR1A membrane localization.

cited_title: The BRCA2 is a histone acetyltransferase.
review_notes: The cached abstract explicitly claims intrinsic BRCA2 H3/H4 acetyltransferase activity; PMID:9824164 explicitly reports no evidence for intrinsic amino-terminal HAT activity and identifies P/CAF-associated activity. Complete experiments from both papers are unavailable here, so the competing positive annotations remain unresolved.

cited_title: BRD4 is an atypical kinase that phosphorylates serine2 of the RNA polymerase II carboxy-terminal domain.
review_notes: The normal cache remains abstract-only and explicitly reports direct CTD Ser2 phosphorylation. Previously inspected indexed primary controls are supplementary access, not a complete paper or image audit. The now-cached independent human 1–698 negative result (PMID:24860166) and later mouse-protein positive result (PMID:34688663) leave general intrinsic catalytic attribution disputed; the latter shares investigators with this paper. Physical CTD association is a separate supported claim.

cited_title: Brd4 activates P-TEFb for RNA polymerase II CTD phosphorylation.
review_notes: Normal full XML cache: abstract, relevant Methods and the negative kinase paragraph were read. Human BRD4 residues 1–698 produced in E. coli or Sf21 showed no phosphorylation under the reported conditions; the authors allow additional preparation or activation requirements. Its principal P-TEFb activation experiments concern a separate recruited-kinase mechanism. DISPUTED identifies this paper as the counterweight in unresolved general BRD4 kinase attribution, not a claim that its bounded negative observation is invalid. Supplementary images and raw biochemical data were not independently inspected.

cited_title: The intrinsic kinase activity of BRD4 spans its BD2-B-BID domains.
review_notes: Normal full XML cache: abstract and relevant Results/construct and kinase Methods were read. Positive assays use mouse full-length 1400-aa BRD4 and truncations, including CTD phosphorylation by WT and residues 1–730; smaller fragments and substrate-binding requirements are distinguished. This is not an independent-laboratory replication of the 2012 report because investigators overlap. Human-fragment negative results in PMID:24860166 leave species/preparation-dependent attribution unresolved. No clean point-mutant separation of intrinsic kinase and recruitment functions or raw figure audit is claimed.

cited_title: Mitochondrial BTD hydrolyses BCTN
review_notes: The actual Reactome mitochondrial hydrolysis claim is verified as a database assertion, but the cited localization evidence does not establish an active human matrix pool. The general molecular function is independently supported.

cited_title: Defective mitochondrial BTD does not hydrolyse BCTN
review_notes: The disease reaction inherits the uncertain mitochondrial compartment. A loss-of-function model is not independent evidence for that wild-type location; BTD catalytic function itself is established.

cited_title: BubR1 phosphorylates CENP-E as a switch enabling the transition from lateral association to end-on capture of spindle microtubules.
review_notes: Selected complete Results and Methods directly inspected: human Sf9-derived BUBR1, K795A/D911A/D882N controls, CENP-E Ser2639 assays and BRT-1-resistant rescue. These are substantial positive catalytic evidence, distinct from the Drosophila crystal structure and human computational model. The negative human-domain/IP primary results remain unreconciled; DISPUTED records that conflict rather than a retraction or proof of contamination.

cited_title: The vertebrate mitotic checkpoint protein BUBR1 is an unusual pseudokinase.
review_notes: Complete normal cached abstract read; it remains abstract-only. Supplemental primary institutional PDF text was read in Results (PDF pages 4–5) and Methods (page 8): https://www.hubrecht.eu/app/uploads/2017/11/Kops_Research_2012_Suijkerbuijk_The-vertebrate-mitotic-checkpoint-protein-BUBR1-is-an-unusual-psuedokinase.pdf. Human bacterial kinase-domain negative assays, active BUB1 controls and cellular immunoprecipitate controls are distinct from positive Sf9 preparations. Images were not independently analyzed. Dispensability is not an absence claim.

cited_title: Structure of complement receptor 2 in complex with its C3d ligand.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract establishes a C3d-CR2 complex. The later PMID:21527715 disputes the earlier binding interface, potentially influenced by crystallization zinc, while retaining the interaction itself. Do not treat the old interface as settled.

cited_title: The chemoattractant receptor-like protein C5L2 binds the C3a des-Arg77/acylation-stimulating protein.
review_notes: Complete cached positive ASP/C5L2-binding abstract read. Independent negative primary binding reports make that mechanism disputed; the listed erratum contents were not inspected, so no retraction or trivial-correction claim is made. The two competing normal caches have now been read and cited in the finding assessment.

cited_title: C5L2 is a functional receptor for acylation-stimulating protein.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract reports human-C5L2 transfection, ASP-associated phosphorylation/arrestin redistribution and metabolic responses. Those observations are separated from the disputed receptor-binding and heterotrimeric G-protein mechanisms. Full original assays were not inspected. Actual normal negative binding/G-protein abstracts are now cited; uncertainty is not merely a missing-cache issue.

cited_title: Isolation of a fragment (C3a) of the third component of human complement containing anaphylatoxin and chemotactic activity and description of an anaphylatoxin inactivator of human serum.
review_notes: Complete cached abstract reports old purified-C3a chemotactic activity. Later original PMID:342601 plus its published correction reports failure to reproduce short-trypsin-C3/C3a leukotaxis and raises possible C5 contamination. Original full old papers were not read; the chemotaxis finding is disputed without dismissing C3a isolation or anaphylatoxin activity.

cited_title: C9ORF72, implicated in amytrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia, regulates endosomal trafficking.
review_notes: Complete abstract and selected canonical Methods/Results were inspected. Its endogenous sc-138763 labeling is challenged by later knockout-specificity testing (PMID:30075745), while tagged constructs and trafficking perturbations require separate assessment. The ddx309 correction replaces Fig. 5E internalized-TrkB imagery and restores Fig. 7C legend text; authors state conclusions unchanged. Correction prose, not corrected image reanalysis, was read. Canonical and authenticated alternate Full Text bodies match.

cited_title: Loss of C9ORF72 impairs autophagy and synergizes with polyQ Ataxin-2 to induce motor neuron dysfunction and cell death.
review_notes: Canonical cache is abstract-only. Authenticated fuller normal-fetch HTML supplied selected complex co-IP, Sf9 purification, GDP-release, Rab39B-rescue and Methods passages. Those are genuine positive complex GEF data requiring reconciliation with later GAP-focused work; they are not dismissed from domain nomenclature. Quotes use only canonical text.

cited_title: A C9ORF72/SMCR8-containing complex regulates ULK1 and plays a dual role in autophagy.
review_notes: Complete abstract and selected purification/exchange Results and Methods were read. Rab39B exchange was measured with complex preparations; this must be distinguished from an autonomous C9orf72 assay and reconciled with later GAP-focused studies. SMCR8 transcriptional or kinase-regulatory functions are not simply inherited by C9orf72.

cited_title: Gabapentin receptor alpha2delta-1 is a neuronal thrombospondin receptor responsible for excitatory CNS synaptogenesis.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Cell 2009). The origin of the thrombospondin-receptor/synaptogenesis model. Correctly cited and highly influential, but the claim is contested - a 2025 presynaptic triple conditional knockout found synapse development intact. Note that the original claim was specifically postsynaptic, so the 2025 presynaptic result narrows it rather than overturning it outright. Not used to support any annotation in this file.

cited_title: Caspase-4 binds to LPS membranes with positive curvature for non-canonical inflammasome activation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Immunity 2026, Broz lab); abstract-only in cache, full text not retrieved. Correctly cited, but its central claim - that caspase-4 engages LPS membranes of defined geometry rather than individual LPS molecules - is in tension with the direct LPS/lipid A binding measurements underlying the GO:0001530 IDAs and with the 2026 HDX-MS pocket mapping. Flagged as DISPUTED for that reason, not because of any citation defect.

cited_title: Human non-canonical inflammasomes activate CASP3 to limit intracellular Salmonella replication in macrophages.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (PLoS Pathog 2026); full text cached from PMC and quotes checked verbatim. The CASP3/CASP7 substrate claim is direct biochemistry but single-source, and the accompanying claim that most GSDMD cleavage in non-canonical signalling is CASP1-mediated is a cell-context flux argument that cuts against the widely reproduced CASP4-GSDMD axis. Contested rather than miscited.

cited_title: c-Abl tyrosine kinase regulates caspase-9 autocleavage in the apoptotic response to DNA damage.
review_notes: Supports the original c-Abl/Tyr-153 DNA-damage model for CASP9, but the Tyr-153 phosphorylation claim is challenged by PMID:29066624, which found no Tyr-153 phosphorylation and instead identified inhibitory Tyr-397 phosphorylation.

cited_title: CDH23: catenin, neuronal and calcium process scope
review_notes: Full report read. Correctly distinguishes colocalization from binding and identifies the PMCA2 assay context. However, its repeated claim that PMID:30747484 contains no catenin mentions is contradicted by the full-text Results and Discussion. Absence of human neuronal experiments does not refute the inherited process, and a structural contributor need not itself pump calcium.

cited_title: Focused Primary-Evidence Audit: Human CFAP410 (O43822) Subcellular Localization for GO Curation
review_notes: Useful secondary audit corroborating the independently checked Bai2011 source mismatch. Several recommendations exceed the evidence: it equates unsupported PM source attribution with a biologically contradicted location; proposes outer-segment remapping from abstract wording; treats locally available Fang full text as inaccessible; summarizes HPA without its per-location/antibody limitations; and calls the 2023 complex paper association-only despite its functional and localization experiments. Only claims checked against primary sources are adopted.

cited_title: OpenScientist hypothesis investigation - CRMP1 cyclic-amide hydrolase activity
review_notes: The residue-loss analysis and primary CRMP2 structural evidence substantiate loss of the ancestral cyclic-amide reaction. The report overstates that no CRMP has any catalytic activity (the CRMP3/DPYSL4 HDAC report PMID:23443259 is a counterexample needing assessment), and cannot establish that abstract-only PMID:8973361 contains no assay anywhere in its full text. Its author attribution of PMID:28044206 and PMID:25358863 is incorrect; canonical cached records identify Myllykoski et al. and Nakamura et al. respectively. A distinct CRMP1 metabolic BP must not be excluded solely from catalytic loss.

cited_title: Early emergence of negative regulation of the tyrosine kinase Src by the C-terminal Src kinase.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (esummary title match). Only the abstract was read; its conclusion conflicts with PMID:18390552 and PMID:16873552 on whether premetazoan Csk inhibits Src.

cited_title: DNER acts as a neuron-specific Notch ligand during Bergmann glial development.
review_notes: The cached abstract directly supports the Bergmann-glial phenotype and proposed Deltex-dependent/RBP-J-independent signaling, but its claim that DNER binds and activates NOTCH1 was not reproduced in PMID:27622512.

cited_title: OpenScientist assessment of CRMP3 deacetylase and broad hydrolase activity
review_notes: Read entire report and compared Methods/Results to the full primary article. Enzyme-attribution and replication uncertainties are useful, but full-length constructs were tested; HEK293 and Sf9 tags/purification differ; TSA sensitivity does not demonstrate contamination; NOT dihydropyrimidinase does not negate parent hydrolase terms. Exact reported sequence identities/residue maps lack delivered code or alignment artifacts and are not adopted as independently verified measurements.

cited_title: OpenScientist focused report on EIF2AK3/PERK nuclear localization
review_notes: The report usefully identifies HPA nucleoplasm immunofluorescence and the full-length ER-membrane topology. Its assertion that GO:0005634 excludes the nuclear envelope is false: GO:0005635 is part_of GO:0005634 (AmiGO verified 2026-09-20). Absence of direct annotations and primary ER residence do not refute an ancestral IBA. HPA CAB009204 has standard Approved ICC, not enhanced genetic or orthogonal validation; the signal is supporting evidence with unresolved specificity, not an established artifact.

cited_title: OpenScientist assessment of EIF4E2 and the eIF4F complex under hypoxia
review_notes: Full narrative and delivered plot provenance code read. Supported initiation/repression findings retained. The complex-composition rejection overlooks primary endogenous eIF4E2/eIF4A/eIF4G3 pull-downs and depletion evidence in PMID:26854219 and eIF4A recruitment in PMID:22678294. The report also conflates cap-pocket stacking residues with the opposite dorsal partner-binding surface and labels IBA/ISS evidence weak without evaluating the ancestral assertion. Plot code hard-codes claimed sequence identities rather than delivering the alignment, so exact numbers are not adopted as reproduced analyses.

cited_title: N6-methyladenosine in nuclear RNA is a major substrate of the obesity-associated FTO.
review_notes: The in vitro m6A demethylation is not in question and the paper is correctly cited. Its central inference - that nuclear mRNA m6A is the major physiological substrate - is what the direct-sequencing reassessment (PMID:41279954) and the m6Am literature contest.

cited_title: Dynamic m(6)A mRNA methylation directs translational control of heat shock response.
review_notes: Correctly cited and a genuine mutant-phenotype experiment, but the m6A readout is antibody-based, which is the methodology under challenge. It is the IMP leg of the contested GO:1990931 annotation.

cited_title: Structure-Based Design of a Highly Potent Dual-Competitive FTO Inhibitor for Targeted m(6)A Demethylase Inhibition in AML.
review_notes: Representative of the active drug-discovery literature that assumes the m6A-eraser model. Cited here to show that side of the dispute is current, not superseded. Its cellular m6A readouts are antibody-based, and the claim that FTO inhibitors act through FTO is exactly what PMID:41279954 challenges. Cached record is abstract-only.

cited_title: Histone tyrosine sulfation by SULT1B1 regulates H4R3me2a and gene transcription.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2023;19:855-864). Defines the H3Y99sulf mark that PMID:41686426 later attributes to GAL3ST1, and attributes it to a different enzyme (SULT1B1). Formally contested by PMID:40890505; the authors replied (PMID:40890506) and an Author Correction was issued (PMID:40890508). Not retracted. Cited only to document the dispute; no GAL3ST1 annotation derives from it.

cited_title: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nat Chem Biol 2025;21:1667-1670), full text available via PMC12978989. A formal Matters Arising arguing that the H3Y99sulf spectra fit a phosphotyrosine peptide, that sulfotyrosine cannot give the reported 100% sulfate-retaining HCD fragments, and that recombinant enzyme gave no histone H3.2 sulfation. Bears on GAL3ST1 because it questions the existence of the mark and the specificity of the antibody used to detect it. Marked DISPUTED because the original authors contest it, not because of any citation problem.

cited_title: Reply to: Mass spectrometry and enzyme assays refute histone tyrosine sulfation.
